answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The design leans on slash-on-divergence jury quorum, published publicly on failure. What survives to the forge is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Work waits on the walnut until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the atlas of the next round.
